# WHAT MOVES INTO THE STORE

```

final _scopeRecordWrites = <String, Completer<void>>{};
```

which builds `ConnectedDeviceRecordStore(database, storageService)` internally.

## Suggested store API (rename to these names; keep bodies identical)
```dart

bool get hasPersistence;                                      // see NULL SEMANTICS below
List<ConnectedDeviceRecord>? recordsOf(String scopeKey);      // was `_scopeRecords[scopeKey]`

bool isLoaded(String scopeKey);                               // was `_loadedScopes.contains`

Future<Result<void>> ensureDatabase();                        // was `_databaseInitialization ??= _database!.initialize()`
Future<Result<ConnectedDevicePersistenceSnapshot>> load(String scopeKey); // was `_store.load(scopeKey)`
Future<bool> persistRecords(String scopeKey, List<ConnectedDeviceRecord> devices, {bool Function()? isCurrent});
                                                              // was `_enqueueScopeRecordWrite(scopeKey, () => _store.saveRecords(...))`

ConnectedDeviceRecord? recordFor(String? deviceId, {required List<ConnectedDeviceRecord> fallback});
ConnectedDeviceRecord? recordForTarget(String scopeKey, String deviceId, {String? hardwareAddress, required List<ConnectedDeviceRecord> fallback});
static bool sameRecord(ConnectedDeviceRecord item, String deviceId, String? hardwareAddress);

```
Notes:
- `_recordFor` and `_recordForTarget` currently read `_recordsForScope(_accountScope.storageKey)` implicitly. Change them to take `scopeKey` explicitly (as above) and pass `_accountScope.storageKey` (or the appropriate scope key) from the controller call sites. Also pass `fallback: state` where the controller call site needs the in-memory fallback — `_recordsForScope`'s fallback was `_recordStore == null ? state : const []`, so the controller must supply that fallback expression at the call site. Keep the exact same fallback semantics per call site.
- `recordFor`/`recordForTarget`/`sameRecord` in the store must not read `ref` or `state`.

## `_stageScopeRecords` special case
The controller keeps a method `_stageScopeRecords` that must do exactly what it does today:
```dart
void _stageScopeRecords(String scopeKey, List<ConnectedDeviceRecord> records) {
  _scopes.stage(scopeKey, records);   // data
  _publishScopeRecords(scopeKey);     // still publishes state, stays in controller
}
```

## `_save` STAYS in the controller
Its optimistic-stage + rollback + publish sequencing must be preserved. Only its inner call `_enqueueScopeRecordWrite(scopeKey, () => _store.saveRecords(scopeKey, devices, isCurrent: isCurrent))` becomes `_scopes.persistRecords(scopeKey, devices, isCurrent: isCurrent)`, and `_resultValue(...)` becomes `ConnectedDeviceScopeStore.resultValue(...)` (or a private helper).

## `_ensurePersistenceReady` (2241-2285) STAYS in the controller
Rewrite only its store accesses: `_loadedScopes.contains(scopeKey)` -> `_scopes.isLoaded(scopeKey)`; `_databaseInitialization ??= _database!.initialize()` -> `await _scopes.ensureDatabase()`; `_loadedScopes.add(scopeKey); _scopeRecords[scopeKey] = value.records;` -> `_scopes.markLoaded(scopeKey, value.records);`; `_store.load(scopeKey)` -> `_scopes.load(scopeKey)`. Keep all `connectedDevicePersistenceProvider` calls, `ref.mounted` checks and ordering identical.

# NULL SEMANTICS — THE MOST IMPORTANT PART
Seven test subclasses override `build()` and do NOT call `super.build()`, e.g.:
`class _EmptyConnectedDevices extends ConnectedDevicesController { @override List<ConnectedDeviceRecord> build() => const []; }`
They rely on the old `_recordStore == null` / `_database == null` state to mean "this controller has no persistence, fall back to in-memory `state`".

So in the controller keep:
```dart
ConnectedDeviceScopeStore? _scopeStore;
```
created ONLY inside the real `build()`:
```dart
_scopeStore ??= ConnectedDeviceScopeStore(
  database: ref.read(localDatabaseProvider),
  storageService: ref.read(storageServiceProvider),
);
```
(the `??=` preserves today's create-once-across-rebuilds behavior).
Then:
- every old `_recordStore == null` / `_database == null` test becomes `_scopeStore == null`
- every old `_store.` use becomes `_scopes.records.` where `_scopes` is a private getter `ConnectedDeviceScopeStore get _scopes => _scopeStore!;`
- `_scopeStore == null` must still be checked BEFORE touching `_scopes` in: `awaitPersistenceReady` (~line 70-76), `_recordsForScope` fallback path, and wherever `_recordStore` is tested at lines ~1106, ~1126, ~1164, ~2236. Read each site and preserve its exact intent.

# Smart Device Platform — Agent Guide

Short entry point for coding agents. Use this file for start-up discipline only; detailed rules live in [`harness/`](harness/), project navigation lives in [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md).

## Project Overview

Flutter monorepo for smart-device Apps such as glasses, watches, and earphones. App-specific behavior
stays in Apps. Shared capabilities enter Foundation only when they meet the ownership and Spec
admission rules; qualifying contracts precede Foundation implementation.

```text
apps/              App shells, brand and App-specific logic
packages/widget/   Reusable or cross-Feature UI composition outside an owning Feature
packages/feature/  Complete user scenarios, grouped by domain (device/, ai/, …)
packages/common/   Shared primitives below Feature (no Feature deps)
packages/core/     Platform-neutral base types and reusable capability contracts
packages/platform/ Native SDK artifacts, bridges and platform lifecycle adapters
specs/             Capability contracts
```

Dependencies use only permitted public APIs. Apps may depend directly on any lower layer; Widget,
Feature, and Common boundaries follow
[`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md#layer-structure). A Feature may consume another
Feature's public contract only through a single-direction, cycle-free dependency under
[`ADR-0010`](docs/decisions/0010-feature-dependencies.md). Core and Platform are peer Foundation
partitions; they may consume each other's public APIs when ownership requires it, while their
combined package graph remains acyclic under
[`ADR-0011`](docs/decisions/0011-platform-device-runtime.md).

## Fact Priority

Use each source for the fact it owns:

- Code and `pubspec.yaml` describe current implementation and dependencies. Passing tests provide
  evidence only for the behavior they exercise.
- `stable` Specs define adopted public capability contracts.
- `active` Specs define evolving contracts under adoption; they do not prove delivery.
- Accepted ADRs define architecture decisions and require a superseding ADR to change. Current
  architecture documents describe the adopted model and must remain consistent with them.
- Device, platform, SDK, backend, parity, and runtime claims require traceable runtime evidence.
- Draft Specs, Plans, and `app_configs/` describe intent only.

When sources disagree about the same fact, use status, chronology, and explicit supersession to
resolve them. Follow [`docs/INDEX.md`](docs/INDEX.md#fact-priority) and report unresolved material
conflicts instead of silently selecting a convenient source.

`app_configs/` remains planning input for existing Apps and does not participate in their manual
builds. `tool/app_assembly.dart` is the implemented generator/validator for explicitly admitted v1
configs; it does not replace the checked-in `apps/` shells or make `generate_app.dart` a capability.

## Independent Judgment

* Before accepting a request's premise or proposed solution, check for false assumptions, logical
  gaps, missing context, and unsupported conclusions.
* Distinguish verified facts, evidence-based inferences, uncertain assumptions, and subjective
  judgments. Verify material figures, entities, and conclusions against traceable sources when
  relevant and practical.
* Do not optimize for agreement. When evidence contradicts the proposed direction, state the
  disagreement directly and explain the basis, risks, overlooked variables, costs, biases, and
  credible alternatives.
* Do not expand the task merely to eliminate every uncertainty. Surface material uncertainty and
  ask or investigate further only when it could meaningfully change the implementation or outcome.
